content.title: About
content.content: Cheese spread and cream cheese are soft dairy products made by curdling milk and then blending the resulting curd with additives such as butter, cream, or seasonings. They have a mild creamy flavor, a smooth texture, and are widely used as a spread, sauce ingredient, or filling.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Cream cheese originated in the United States in the early 20th century as a cheaper alternative to traditional cottage cheese.
In Russia, the popularity of cheese spread surged in the 2010s due to the growing demand for ready‑to‑eat snacks.
Cream cheese is a key ingredient in cheesecakes, giving the filling its characteristic smoothness.
Various flavorings are added, such as herbs, smoked salmon, garlic, and pepper.
When unopened, cream cheese can be stored in the refrigerator for up to 4 weeks past the printed date.

items.title: Source of calcium
items.content: Cream cheese provides calcium, which is essential for bone and teeth health.

items.title: Rich in protein
items.content: Its protein content helps maintain muscle mass and promotes satiety.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: The product contains vitamins B2 and B12, which support energy metabolism.

items.title: Low lactose content
items.content: Most lactose is removed during fermentation, making it tolerable for many people with mild lactose intolerance.

items.title: Probiotic cultures
items.content: Some cheese spreads are fortified with live cultures that support gut microbiota.

items.title: Milk protein allergy
items.content: Individuals allergic to casein or whey proteins may react to cream cheese.

items.title: High sodium
items.content: Certain varieties contain a lot of salt, which can be problematic for hypertension.

items.title: Fat content
items.content: Cream cheese is high in saturated fats; consumption should be moderate.

items.title: Shelf‑life after opening
items.content: Once opened, the product loses freshness quickly; keep it sealed and respect the use‑by date.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Spread cheese on bread, crackers, use in sandwiches, mix into sauces, casseroles, and salads. It is often combined with herbs, spices, or smoked salmon for extra flavor.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the spread in the refrigerator at 2‑6 °C in its original packaging or an airtight container. After opening, consume within 2‑3 weeks. Discard if it develops off‑odors, mold, or discoloration.

chicken-leg-drumstick-and-thigh-rotisser.title: Chicken leg, drumstick and thigh, rotisserie, skin not eaten

content.title: About
content.content: Chicken legs, drumsticks and thighs prepared on a rotisserie without skin are a lean source of protein. The rotisserie method keeps the meat juicy while the removal of skin reduces fat and calorie content.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Dark meat contains more iron than white breast meat.
Rotisserie cooking ensures even heat distribution and enhances spice flavor.
Skin‑less portions contain less than 2 % saturated fat by weight.
Chicken is a good source of vitamin B6, which supports amino‑acid metabolism.
These cuts are traditionally used in Asian and Mediterranean dishes.

items.title: Rich source of protein
items.content: A 100‑g serving provides about 20 g of high‑quality protein needed for tissue growth and repair.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: Without skin the fat content drops to 3‑4 g per 100 g, making it suitable for low‑fat diets.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Contains vitamin B12, niacin (B3) and pyridoxine (B6) which support nervous system function and energy metabolism.

items.title: Minerals
items.content: Provides iron, zinc and phosphorus, important for blood formation, immunity and bone health.

items.title: Low glycemic index
items.content: Does not cause a rapid rise in blood glucose, which is beneficial for people with diabetes.

items.title: Poultry allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to chicken proteins.

items.title: Bacterial contamination
items.content: Insufficient cooking can leave salmonella or campylobacter alive.

items.title: Added sodium in processed versions
items.content: If the product is pre‑marinated, watch the salt content.

items.title: Cholesterol content
items.content: Even without skin, chicken meat contains cholesterol; people with hypercholesterolemia should monitor portions.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the rotisserie pieces hot, add them to salads, soups, or stir‑fries. They can be sliced and sautéed with vegetables or tossed into pasta. A squeeze of lemon and a sprinkle of fresh herbs enhance flavor.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep refrigerated at 0‑4 °C in an airtight container for 3‑4 days. For longer storage freeze at ‑18 °C; thaw in the refrigerator, not at room temperature.

content.title: About
content.content: Chicken is one of the most widely consumed meats worldwide. It can be baked, grilled, roasted, or boiled. Chicken meat is rich in protein and provides B‑vitamins, iron, and zinc. The skin is edible but is often removed to reduce fat content.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Chicken was domesticated over 8,000 years ago in Southeast Asia.
The most popular part is the breast because it contains the least fat.
Chicken bones are used to make broth, which is high in collagen.
More than 100 million tonnes of chicken are consumed globally each year.
Chicken eggs are a major source of protein and vitamins.

items.title: High‑quality protein
items.content: Chicken provides all essential amino acids, making it an excellent source of complete protein.

items.title: Low fat (especially skinless breast)
items.content: Skinless breast meat contains very little saturated fat, suitable for low‑fat diets.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Chicken is rich in niacin (B3) and vitamin B6, which support metabolism and nervous system health.

items.title: Minerals
items.content: It supplies iron, zinc, and selenium, important for immune function and antioxidant protection.

items.title: Supports muscle mass
items.content: The high protein content helps build and repair muscle, especially for active individuals.

items.title: Food‑borne illness risk
items.content: Undercooked chicken may contain Salmonella or Campylobacter, so it should be cooked to an internal temperature of 75 °C.

items.title: Allergy
items.content: Some people may be allergic to chicken meat or eggs.

items.title: Sodium in processed products
items.content: Smoked or marinated chicken often contains high levels of salt, which is undesirable for hypertension.

items.title: Skin fat content
items.content: Chicken skin is high in saturated fat; excessive consumption can raise cholesterol levels.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Chicken can be grilled, baked, boiled, fried, or stewed. Breast meat is commonly used in salads, sandwiches, and low‑fat dishes, while thighs add juiciness to braised recipes. The skin can be crisped and added to soups or salads for texture.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Fresh chicken should be kept in the refrigerator for no more than 2 days. Frozen chicken lasts up to 9 months at –18 °C. Rinse and pat dry before cooking. Do not leave chicken at room temperature for more than 2 hours.

macaroni-or-pasta-salad-with-tuna.title: Macaroni or Pasta Salad with Tuna

content.title: About
content.content: Macaroni or pasta salad with tuna is a cold dish where cooked pasta (usually short shapes like elbows or penne) is mixed with canned tuna, vegetables, and a light dressing made from mayonnaise, yogurt, or olive oil. It is popular as a quick, nutritious meal for lunch, picnics, or snacks.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The pasta salad became popular in the United States in the mid‑20th century as a convenient picnic food.
Canned tuna retains most of its nutrients, including omega‑3 fatty acids.
Variations may include corn, peas, olives, feta cheese, or fresh herbs.
The recipe can be adapted for dietary needs by swapping mayonnaise for yogurt to lower calories.
Whole‑grain pasta versions increase the fiber content of the dish.

items.title: High in protein
items.content: Tuna provides high‑quality protein essential for tissue growth and repair.

items.title: Omega‑3 fatty acids
items.content: Tuna supplies EPA and DHA, which support heart health and reduce inflammation.

items.title: Carbohydrates for energy
items.content: Pasta offers quickly digestible carbs that fuel active days.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Both tuna and whole‑grain pasta provide B1, B2, B3, and B6 vitamins important for metabolism.

items.title: Minerals
items.content: The dish contains iron, magnesium, and selenium, which aid immunity and thyroid function.

items.title: Fish allergy
items.content: Tuna can trigger allergic reactions in individuals sensitive to seafood.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Canned tuna is often salty; low‑sodium versions are recommended for those limiting salt intake.

items.title: Food‑borne illness risk
items.content: Improper storage above 4 °C for more than 2 hours may allow bacterial growth.

items.title: Mercury
items.content: Tuna may contain trace amounts of mercury; pregnant women and children should limit consumption.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the salad chilled as a standalone dish or as a side to meat or fish. It is convenient to pack in a container for lunch or a picnic. For extra freshness, add chopped vegetables, herbs, or a squeeze of lemon juice.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the salad in an airtight container in the refrigerator at 0–4 °C for up to 3 days. Stir before serving to redistribute the dressing. Discard if it develops an off‑odor or discoloration.

tea-iced-instant-green-pre-sweetened-wit.title: Iced Instant Green Tea, Pre‑sweetened with Low‑Calorie Sweetener

content.title: About
content.content: Iced instant green tea is a convenient way to quickly prepare a refreshing beverage. The tea is brewed, dried and packed into single‑serve sachets, then sweetened with a low‑calorie sweetener, giving it a sweet taste without added sugar.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Green tea is rich in polyphenols, which have antioxidant properties.
Instant tea retains most of the beneficial compounds of whole leaf tea.
Low‑calorie sweeteners reduce the drink’s energy content while preserving flavor.
Iced tea is especially popular in summer as a quick way to cool down.
Portion‑pack packaging makes transport and storage easy.

items.title: Antioxidant protection
items.content: Polyphenols in green tea help neutralize free radicals, supporting cellular health.

items.title: Metabolism support
items.content: Green tea extracts may help boost metabolism and aid fat oxidation.

items.title: Low calorie
items.content: The low‑calorie sweetener allows a sweet taste with minimal added calories.

items.title: Hydration
items.content: Iced tea provides fluid intake, especially useful in hot weather.

items.title: Convenient consumption
items.content: The instant format lets you prepare a drink quickly without steeping loose leaves.

items.title: Tea allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to tea components.

items.title: Caffeine sensitivity
items.content: Green tea contains caffeine; people sensitive to it should limit intake.

items.title: Artificial sweeteners
items.content: Certain low‑calorie sweeteners can cause gastrointestinal discomfort in sensitive users.

content.title: How to Use
content.content: Dissolve one sachet in 200–250 ml of cold water, stir until fully dissolved. Optionally add a slice of lemon, mint, or ice.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store sachets in a dry, cool place away from direct sunlight. Once opened, use within 3 months.

content.title: About
content.content: Wheat germ oil is a golden, nutty-smelling oil extracted from the germ of the wheat kernel, the embryo of the grain. It is one of the richest natural food sources of vitamin E. Wheat germ oil is used as a dietary supplement and as a flavorful finishing oil, and it is also used in skin and hair care products.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The wheat germ is the small embryo of the wheat kernel and makes up only a small fraction of its weight.
Wheat germ oil is among the richest natural sources of vitamin E.
It has a strong, nutty flavor and aroma.
It is sensitive to heat and light and is not suitable for frying.
Wheat germ oil is also used in cosmetics and skin care.

items.title: Very rich in vitamin E
items.content: Wheat germ oil is a concentrated source of vitamin E, an antioxidant that helps protect cells.

items.title: Provides polyunsaturated fats
items.content: It contains essential fatty acids, mainly linoleic acid, which the body needs.

items.title: Contains plant compounds
items.content: Wheat germ oil contains plant compounds such as octacosanol and phytosterols that are being studied.

items.title: Easy to add to foods
items.content: A small amount can be added to smoothies, yogurt, or dressings.

items.title: Used in skin care
items.content: Applied topically, it is used as a moisturizing oil.

items.title: Wheat allergy and gluten
items.content: Wheat germ oil is derived from wheat and may contain traces of wheat protein. People with wheat allergy or celiac disease should consult a healthcare professional before using it.

items.title: Possible medication interactions
items.content: High intakes of vitamin E may affect blood clotting. People taking blood thinners should consult a healthcare professional.

items.title: Rancidity
items.content: The oil spoils easily, and rancid oil should not be used.

items.title: Skin reactions
items.content: Applied to the skin, it may cause irritation or allergic reactions in some people. Do a patch test first.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Wheat germ oil is best used cold, drizzled over salads, stirred into smoothies, yogurt, or oatmeal, or used in dressings. Do not heat it or use it for frying, since heat damages its nutrients and flavor. Use only small amounts, since it is calorie-dense.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store wheat germ oil in a tightly closed dark bottle in the refrigerator after opening and keep it away from heat and light. Use it within the time given on the label. Discard oil that smells bitter, sharp, or like paint.
